text:
Predicates:
Costs(test, amount) ::: The test costs amount.
Cheaper(amount1, amount2) ::: amount1 is cheaper than amount2.
Provides(organization, aid, applicant) ::: organization provides aid to applicant.
FinancialAid(applicant) ::: applicant receives financial aid.
ProveHardship(applicant) ::: applicant can prove economic hardship.
SingleParentFamily(person) ::: person lives in a single-parent family.
FewResources(person) ::: person has few resources available to them.
Applying(person, test) ::: person is applying to take test.
Premises:
Costs(gre, 205) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test.
Cheaper(205, 300) ::: $205 is cheaper than $300.
∀x (Applicant(x) ∧ ProveHardship(x) → Provides(ets, financialAid, x)) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those GRE applicants who prove economic hardship.
∀x ((SingleParentFamily(x) ∨ FewResources(x)) → ProveHardship(x)) ::: Those living in single-parent families or having few resources available to them can prove economic hardship.
SingleParentFamily(tom) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family.
FewResources(tom) ::: Tom has few resources available to him.
Applying(tom, gre) ::: Tom is applying to take the GRE test.
Conclusion:
¬∃x (Applying(x, gre) ∧ ∃y (Provides(y, financialAid, x) ∧ y ≠ ets)) ::: No one taking the GRE test has financial aid provided to them by something.
